newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks close near record high.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks close near record high.

text.p: The Australian share market came near to setting a record closing high on Friday after major resource issues were buoyed by stronger metal prices.
The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 13.3 points higher at 2,336.8, just 3.8 points short of its record closing high of 2,340.6.
The December share price index contract ended 12 points up at 2,359 and at a 22.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said investors were encouraged by a rally in copper and aluminium prices on Thursday with rises by key blue chip resource groups BHP, CRA and WMC underpinning the market's gain.
"I think it was a fairly admirable performance from the market today given there were no positive leads from offshore equity markets," a Brisbane-based dealer said.

The dealer said decent gains by most base metals on the London Metal Exchange was the principal factor behind the market's rise, particularly the price of copper which he said was starting to show signs of stability after a prolonged fall.
"BHP lost ground at the end of the day but its strength for most of the session gave the market a good deal of confidence," the dealer said.

Major resource issues ended firm but off early highs after base metal prices showed signs of a recovery and after weak jobs data on Thursday put downward pressure on the local currency.
*Woolworths A$2.78 (+.03) 2.76/2.80 Vol: 1,756,492 Retailer said its Q1 sales rose 8.24 pct to A$3.85 billion.
Gold producer's shares continued to rise after the company announced a major new gold discovery at its Darlot mine in Western Australia on Thursday.

*C-C Amatil A$18.00 (+.21) 17.737/18.15 Vol: 1,202,903 Food and beverage group continued to benefit from its alliance with Malaysian tycoon's Robert Kuok's Kerry Group and a roadshow by senior executives, dealers said.
Brokers said U.S. inflation and retail sales data due out later today could have a big impact on Wall Street which would likely set the direction of Australian shares early next week.

The stock of food and beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil continued to run higher with dealers citing the company's alliance with Malaysian tycoon, Robert Kuok and a roadshow by senior executives as the main reasons for its outperformance.
Gold miner Plutonic Resources was another outstanding issue, the company's stock continuing to rise strongly after it announced a significant discovery at its Darlot gold mine in Western Australia.
In other markets, Australian bonds ended softer in line with a fourth successive weaker close on U.S. Treasuries.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.59 percent, up 0.03 percent from Thursday's closing level.
The Australian dollar remained trapped within a tight range with the unit showing resilience to rate cut speculation. At 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7892/97.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade remained buoyant however futures trade was more cautiuos ahead of key U.S. economic data.
Total options traded 42,454 (38,771).
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 4,905 (7,420).
